endorsements.quote: From this we derive a "Three-Tiered Liability Escalation Framework" (T-LEF) that allocates accountability among AI developers, healthcare institutions, and clinicians according to measurable degrees of autonomy.
We therefore propose that the policy framework treat algorithmic traceability as a necessary complement to algorithmic explainability, rather than as a replacement for it.

Drawing on systematic-review evidence that clinician verification effort decreases monotonically as system acceptance rates rise ( 20 ), we propose, provisionally, that a Tier 2 system exhibiting clinician acceptance above 95 percent across a clinically significant denominator should trigger mandatory reclassification review under Tier 3.
Human-Factors Testing : Evidence of pre-deployment evaluation under realistic clinical workflow conditions, including studies of alert fatigue, automation bias, and clinician override behavior.

Independent Pre-deployment Validation : Performance evaluation by an entity organizationally and financially independent of the developer, using a clearly described clinical validation set during the interim phase and, once available, a publicly governed standardized CDH benchmark.

Incident Reporting and Model-Update Documentation : Mandatory reporting of clinically significant adverse events through MAUDE or equivalent national registries, and full version-controlled documentation of all model updates including the safety evaluation associated with each update.

Correspondingly, independent pre-deployment validation and, once available, standardized CDH benchmark datasets should include adequately powered paediatric strata spanning the neonatal-to-adolescent range.

The transparency-disclosure element (Section 5 ) should require paediatric-stratified CDH rates rather than aggregate figures, because adult-pooled performance can mask poor paediatric performance given the data asymmetries noted above.

unlisted_practices: Establish a cryptographically secured, privacy-preserving Clinical Algorithmic Audit Trail recording model provenance, RAG citation log, prompt and output record, confidence metadata, and clinician interaction metadata for clinically consequential LLM interactions.
Retain paediatric CAAT records until the patient reaches the age of majority plus the applicable statute-of-limitations period.
Restrict the EHR fields inserted into LLM prompts to the minimum necessary for the clinical query.
Log the EHR fields driving paediatric dosing, such as weight, gestational or postnatal age, and renal and hepatic maturation indices, in tokenized or hashed form.

Allocate legal liability for clinical generative AI according to the system's structural autonomy from meaningful human review, including default patient-facing strict product liability for Tier 3 autonomous systems.
Grant developers a rebuttable presumption of non-defectiveness only upon documented satisfaction of all eight Safe Harbor pre-deployment standards.
Do not grant Safe Harbor protection to systems validated only on adult cases when deployed in paediatric care.
Publicly disclose model-specific clinically deceptive hallucination rates against described validation datasets or standardized benchmarks, updated at least annually.
Implement retrieval-augmented generation with verifiable source grounding as an architectural safeguard, recognizing it is necessary but not sufficient.
Calibrate the threshold for mandatory Tier 3 reclassification review more conservatively for paediatric deployments.
Convene an FDA and EU Commission working group to develop CAAT minimum data standards within 24 months.
Update professional medical association clinical AI governance guidelines to incorporate CDH documentation requirements.
Convene a WHO-mediated process to develop an internationally recognized T-LEF equivalence standard for mutual recognition of liability compliance certifications.
Fund CAAT infrastructure and open-source reference implementations in low- and middle-income countries.
Convene an international consortium to run a five-pathway empirical validation agenda for T-LEF, CDH, CAAT, and Safe Harbor.

screen.reason: This is a hypothesis and theory/framework paper proposing legal liability and ethical traceability frameworks (T-LEF and CAAT) for generative AI in clinical workflows.
